source.note: The buying sequence, verbatim from slide 1586 and slide 1862 — then stripped of every date. Pena's windows were one man's throughput; this is a volume system. Each card states its cadence, its output per run, and the one thing that caps the multiple. Dates appear only inside Pena's verbatim quotes, because that is what he wrote. Nothing the build commits to is expressed in time.

statuses.waiting: Built, waiting on one thing you own
statuses.partial: Half live — some pieces proven, some not
statuses.yours: Yours — the bot cannot do this one for you

order.title: No clock, only volume
order.detail: Twelve steps in Pena's order, each one a lane that runs as often as the system can. A date is a promise someone else has to keep; a rate is a thing you control. Where his quotes contain days, they are quoted, not adopted.

order.title: The ceiling moves to supply
order.detail: Once hours stop binding, what caps the multiple is other people: sellers willing to disclose, chairmen worth asking, lenders with appetite, a mailbox that stays alive. Output is bought with breadth, never with speed.

order.title: Then make it recursive
order.detail: Every reply, verdict and outcome feeds scoring, letters and vertical playbooks, so run 30 beats run 1 at the same cost. That is the only curve that matters here.

workstreams.name: Pick the industry
workstreams.pena_says: QLA COMPLETION TIMELINE: INDUSTRY & IDEA, PLUS ANCHOR CHAIRMAN IN 1ST 30 DAYS
workstreams.cite: slide 1586 · step 1 of the 11 Step Action Plan, slide 1862: "Identify the idea"
workstreams.one_line: One vertical, chosen on evidence, not on what showed up in a search result.
workstreams.bot_does: Normalises every vertical it sees, scans marketplaces and firm sites for what is actually for sale in each, and rejects anything outside the buy-box with a written reason.
workstreams.you_get: 43 listings swept, verticals normalised, every reject carrying a code instead of a shrug — and a shortlist of verticals with real, priced inventory.
workstreams.next: Write the vertical decision into one file so the ICP lives in one place instead of inside a prompt.
workstreams.output_per_run: Every listed business across every source, swept and scored; verticals normalised; every reject carrying a code.
workstreams.ceiling: Source coverage — nothing else. Every source added raises the multiple immediately.

workstreams.name: Write the idea down
workstreams.cite: slide 1862 · on precision: slide 1025 "II Clarify your vision"
workstreams.one_line: Exactly what you are buying, in numbers: vertical, revenue band, geography, the EBITDA multiple you will pay.
workstreams.bot_does: Turns the listing text into a fixed 7-field deal file, scores it on 10 QLA factors, and stamps every unknown as verified, inferred or assumed.
workstreams.you_get: 43 listings → 43 deal files → 11 walker-ready. 32 blocked, and each block names the field that is missing rather than guessing it.
workstreams.next: Target-profile card and cross-source dedupe, so the same business isn't counted twice under two brokers.
workstreams.output_per_run: 43 listings → 43 deal files → 11 walker-ready, per sweep. Repeats as often as the sweep runs.
workstreams.ceiling: Disclosure quality: 32 of 43 die on a missing EBITDA. Unblock asks raise the ceiling; speed does not.

workstreams.name: Anchor the chairman
workstreams.pena_says: INDUSTRY & IDEA, PLUS ANCHOR CHAIRMAN IN 1ST 30 DAYS
workstreams.cite: slide 1586 · step 6 of the seven steps: "IV Creating your Dream Team", slide 1025
workstreams.one_line: One heavyweight who has been where you are going, committed before the board is built around him.
workstreams.bot_does: Defines the chairman role spec, sources candidates who match it, verifies them, and writes the approach. It cannot have the conversation for you.
workstreams.you_get: A named, verified candidate list with a written ask per person — plus the honest gap: the chairman conversation is the one thing Peña kissed frogs over himself.
workstreams.blocker: Your email address + app password (GMAIL_ADDRESS, GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD) to send the approaches
workstreams.next: Send the first wave as soon as mail is on; the court tracker then shows which seats are filled.
workstreams.output_per_run: 40+ verified chairman candidates sourced and approached in one cycle, not one call at a time.
workstreams.ceiling: Reply rate, 20–30% a wave. Volume is the lever — send more waves to more candidates, not faster emails.

workstreams.name: Build the board
workstreams.pena_says: REMAINING DREAM TEAM BOARD MEMBERS, INCLUDING LAWYER, ACCOUNTANT, INDUSTRY EXPERT (S) IN 2ND 30 DAYS
workstreams.one_line: The rest of the seats: directors who give you credibility with sellers and with banks.
workstreams.bot_does: Designs the roster — how many seats, which competencies, in what order — and maps each seat to the specific deal problem it solves.
workstreams.you_get: A board design with a reason per seat, and a roster that shows which seats are still empty.
workstreams.next: Roster filled seat by seat, each with the approach letter and the date it went out.
workstreams.output_per_run: All remaining seats approached in the same cycle as the chairman, verified first.
workstreams.ceiling: Credible names in the vertical — the supply of people worth asking, not the asking.

workstreams.name: Retain the lawyer
workstreams.cite: slide 1586 · step 9 of the seven steps, slide 1025
workstreams.one_line: Top-tier M&A counsel on retainer before you need them, not after a seller sends a contract.
workstreams.bot_does: Targets the firms, finds the partner who actually does deals at your size, verifies the address and writes the approach.
workstreams.you_get: 3 verified counsel targets from the live harvest — though law firms only publish front desks, so the reply is the introduction.
workstreams.next: Wire the retainer tracker so 'engaged' means a signed engagement letter, not an email saying yes.
workstreams.output_per_run: 3 verified counsel firms at partner level per build.
workstreams.ceiling: Firm conflicts and front-desk-only publishing. Law firms hide the partner; the reply is the introduction.

workstreams.name: Retain the accountant
workstreams.cite: slide 1586 · step 8 of the seven steps, slide 1025
workstreams.one_line: A firm large enough that the seller's accountant takes the call, small enough to answer yours.
workstreams.bot_does: Targets large CPA firms, finds named partners where they publish them, and verifies.
workstreams.you_get: 5 verified accountant targets including named partners — jon@, trey@, e.coulter@ — 5/5 MX-checked.
workstreams.next: The QA role: who reads the seller's statements before you sign anything.
workstreams.output_per_run: 5 verified accountant targets per build, named partners where published.
workstreams.ceiling: Named-partner publication. Same engine as counsel, cheaper ask, faster answer.

workstreams.name: Recruit industry experts
workstreams.cite: slide 1586 — named in the same window as counsel and the accountant
workstreams.one_line: Two or three operators who have run or sold companies in this exact vertical.
workstreams.bot_does: Nothing yet — this task did not exist on the board until the timeline named it. Sourcing and approach would reuse the same engine as the chairman.
workstreams.you_get: Honest gap: the source requires them before the offer stage, and the board had no task for it. It has one now (T2.11).
workstreams.blocker: Not built — added to the board this round
workstreams.next: Clone the chairman sourcing path onto a vertical-expert query; the credentials are already the only blocker.
workstreams.output_per_run: Not built yet (T2.11). Reuses the chairman path with a vertical-expert query — same volume from its first run.
workstreams.ceiling: Nothing structural. This lane is empty today, and the sequence says it is required.

workstreams.name: Place your moles
workstreams.pena_says: Not traceable to the slide deck — moles come from chapter 6 of the book.
workstreams.cite: chapter 6 action items in YF100M_FORENSIC_MANUAL.md; explicitly NOT found in qla_usb_slides_full.txt
workstreams.one_line: People inside the industry who tell you what the market is really doing, before you bid.
workstreams.bot_does: Specified only: identify candidates, approach non-transactionally, keep a question bank and an answer ledger with attribution.
workstreams.you_get: Nothing yet — and the citation is thin. This is the one step I cannot put a Peña slide behind.
workstreams.blocker: Source is a chapter-6 fragment, not a quotable slide
workstreams.next: Either find the moles material in the book PDF or demote this step to optional until it is sourced.
workstreams.output_per_run: Specified: candidate ID, non-transactional approach, question bank, answer ledger, reciprocity ledger.
workstreams.ceiling: Trust. This is the one step that cannot be volume-produced — a mole talks because of who you are, not how many you emailed.

workstreams.name: Approach them all
workstreams.pena_says: 7. Action plan (you & other decision makers) a. Get others obsessed b. Walk your talk (never ever share doubt)
workstreams.cite: slide 1862 · on persistence: slide 2158 — "You must kiss a lot of frogs! Period!"
workstreams.one_line: One written approach per firm, on two channels: email where published, form where not.
workstreams.bot_does: Harvests, MX-verifies, renders one role-specific letter per domain, stages addressed .eml files, drives real Chromium on contact forms, then reads every reply and classifies intent.
workstreams.you_get: 31 verified advisors across four roles, 6 addressed letters staged for one deal, one live form filled end to end (9 fields, screenshot kept).
workstreams.blocker: Sending is waiting on the email credentials; forms run without them
workstreams.next: Rate limits, bounce handling, opt-out — the three things that keep a mailbox alive.
workstreams.output_per_run: 31 verified advisors across four roles; 6 addressed letters staged for one deal; one live form filled end to end with a kept screenshot.
workstreams.ceiling: Mailbox reputation. Rate limits, bounce handling and opt-out are the hard wall — a hard cap on touches per domain, enforced in the ledger.

workstreams.name: Warm the money
workstreams.pena_says: FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS: BANKS, INSURANCE CO'S, PE, ETC, WARMED UP & READY 2 ACCEPT 1ST DEAL IN 3RD 30 DAYS
workstreams.cite: slide 1586 · steps 21–22 of the walker: lender and banker targeting
workstreams.one_line: Lenders opened before the first LOI exists, so the offer is fundable when it is made.
workstreams.bot_does: Targets lenders and bankers at deal size, verifies addresses, writes the ask — what they lend against, what they require personally guaranteed.
workstreams.you_get: 6 verified lender targets including the regional development company that lends at this size. No LOI will be drafted against zero warmed lenders once T2.12 is built.
workstreams.next: Record appetite per lender so the LOI knows its funding before it knows its price.
workstreams.output_per_run: 6 verified lender targets at deal size, approached with the actual deal window stated, before any LOI exists.
workstreams.ceiling: Lender appetite at your size. Offset by breadth: more lenders opened, not a faster application.

workstreams.name: Investigate, search, kiss frogs
workstreams.pena_says: 2. Investigate generalities · 3. Investigate specifics · 6. Investigate continues
workstreams.cite: slides 1862 and 2158 · "Investigation is a search for red flags" (YF100M_FORENSIC_MANUAL.md)
workstreams.one_line: Generalities first, then specifics, then a written search letter to everyone who owns inventory.
workstreams.bot_does: Sweeps red flags at market level, builds the local intel pack, sends search letters, and runs the kiss-frogs loop on everything that survives.
workstreams.you_get: A scored pipeline with reject codes. 32 of 43 blocked today — and the blocks are honest, not papered over.
workstreams.blocker: Deep-dive and red-flag sweep specified, not built
workstreams.next: Build the generality sweep first: one red flag ends the deal, so it should run before the deep dive.
workstreams.output_per_run: Red-flag sweep and local intel pack in minutes; scoring on 10 factors; search letters and the kiss-frogs loop on everything that survives.
workstreams.ceiling: Seller disclosure speed. Only offset is running many deals in parallel instead of waiting on one.

workstreams.name: Offer, close, get paid
workstreams.pena_says: MAKE AN OFFER IN THE 4TH 30 DAYS, OR TOTAL OF 120 DAYS
workstreams.cite: slide 1586 · steps 8–11 of the 11 Step Action Plan, slide 1862: critical path → implementation → execution → re-evaluation
workstreams.one_line: LOI, structure, 1.5x coverage, contract, closing — then pay yourself and your staff first.
workstreams.bot_does: Drafts the LOI, refuses to render it if a money figure was guessed, builds alternative structures and the seller note, tests 1.5x coverage, assembles the contract review pack and closing checklist.
workstreams.you_get: An LOI that will not print with an invented number in it — the one place where refusing to be helpful is the feature.
workstreams.blocker: Negotiation turf, contract review and closing are specified, not built
workstreams.next: Critical path (T6.07) before structure — a timeline that slips is what kills more deals than price.
workstreams.output_per_run: LOI draft, three alternative structures, seller note, the 1.5x coverage test and the contract pack — one session per target.
workstreams.ceiling: Signatures, counsel review, credit decisions. Run ten deals to get ten signatures; one deal cannot move faster than its counterparties.

workstreams.name: The engine room — not in the source
workstreams.pena_says: Not in the source. This is the machine that runs the twelve, and it is labelled as ours.
workstreams.one_line: It wakes repeatedly, refuses to spend money, refuses to send twice, and computes how much outbound it takes to make waiting irrelevant.
workstreams.bot_does: Schedules the cycle, gates credentials, stamps provenance, and (once built) holds single-flight locks, an audit log, dead-letter retry and a kill switch.
workstreams.you_get: Today: a cycle that runs, reports, and queues what needs you. Missing: the locks and audit trail that make it safe to run unattended.
workstreams.next: Single-flight lock, audit log, dead-letter retry, kill switch — every other step's honesty depends on these.
workstreams.output_per_run: A cycle that wakes, sweeps, stages, reads and reports — plus (once built) a send plan that turns a reply-rate target into mailboxes, sends per day and messages in flight.
workstreams.ceiling: Deliverability: per-mailbox send caps, not hours. The governor (T0.11) exists so the multiple is spent where it survives — many mailboxes, many domains, one touch cap.
